title: How Happy Is He Born or Taught
description: How Happy Is He Born or Taught in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Wotton wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 279, “Independence”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How hap-py is he born or taught Who ser-veth not an-oth-er's will; Whose ar-mor is his hon-est thought, And sim-ple truth his high-est skill;

lines: How happy is he born or taught
Whose armor is his honest thought,
And simple truth his highest skill;
Whose passions not his masters are;
Whose soul is still prepared for death;
Not tied unto the world with care
Of public fame or private breath;
Who God doth late and early pray
More of His grace than goods to lend,
And walks with man, from day to day,
As with a brother and a friend!
This man is freed from servile bands
Of hope to rise, or fear to fall;
Lord of himself, though not of lands,
And having nothing, yet hath all.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Henry Wotton died in 1639.
credits: Words by Henry Wotton (1568–1639), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
